title: VIZ_SET2_HEATMAPS_CHARTS.py

canonical_node.axiom: The visualization layer must render the mathematical structure of the LLC (kinetic coupling matrix, symmetry pairs, sensitivity, stability) in a way that is legible to a technical audience without requiring matrix algebra literacy.
definitions: Kinetic coupling matrix: a 10x10 matrix of coupling strengths between the ten variables of the LLC, with diagonal self-coupling weights and off-diagonal symmetry pair couplings (PAIR_STRENGTH = 0.45).
Symmetry pairs: the five pairs (GT, SF, EK, MQ, RC) that are highlighted in the heatmap with distinct colors.
Set 2: the second visualization layer, complementing Set 1 with analytical depth (heatmaps, sensitivity, stability, test results).
derivation: The document describes the kinetic matrix heatmap as the mathematical heart of the LLC, making the coupling structure visible.
The heatmap includes annotations of coupling strength values and symmetry pair highlights, making the structure legible without matrix algebra.
The document states that Set 2 is for the technical audience, to see the coupling structure and follow test results in detail.
The document claims that the kinetic matrix heatmap shows the coupling structure is not arbitrary, with symmetry pairs highlighted against near-zero off-diagonal elements.
canonical_node.action: Generate the described visualizations (kinetic matrix heatmap with annotations and symmetry pair highlights, chi-field time evolution plots, sensitivity analysis charts, stability phase diagram, biblical test results bar charts, coherence collapse scenario comparison) using the specified dark theme (#0a0b0f) and consistent color coding.
boundary: Does not define the mathematical derivation of the kinetic matrix or the LLC equations.
Does not assert that the visualizations prove the underlying theory; they are communication tools.
Does not include interactive features; those are suggestions for website display, not part of the script.
test: Check that the heatmap renders the 10x10 matrix with YlOrBr colormap and overlaid coupling strength values.
Verify that the five symmetry pairs are outlined in the specified colors (red, blue, green, purple, gold).
Verify that the dark theme (#0a0b0f) is consistent across all Set 2 visualizations.
Check that the additional chart types (chi-field evolution, sensitivity, stability, test results, collapse scenarios) are present as described.

dg1_dependencies: LLC mathematical model (kinetic matrix, chi-field, parameter scan results)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides analytical depth visualizations (heatmaps, sensitivity, stability) that complement Set 1's high-impact single images, making the coupling structure and test results visible to a technical audience.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the visual coherence of the project by using the same dark theme and consistent color coding as Set 1.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without Set 2, the project lacks the analytical depth and detailed visualization of the coupling structure, sensitivity, and stability, reducing the ability to communicate the rigor of the results.

overstatement_risks: The document implies the visualizations 'prove' the results were arrived at rigorously, but the visualizations themselves do not constitute proof.
The claim that the coupling structure is 'mathematically derived' is not substantiated in this document; it references the LLC model without derivation.
kill_conditions: If the kinetic matrix or symmetry pairs are not actually derived from the LLC model, the visualizations would be misleading.
If the visualizations are not reproducible from the described script, the artifact loses its utility.
risk.lean_target: A visualization script that accurately renders the LLC coupling structure and analysis charts, without overclaiming proof.

plain_summary: This document describes a Python script for additional visualizations (Set 2) that render the LLC's kinetic coupling matrix as a heatmap with symmetry pair highlights, along with sensitivity, stability, and test result charts. It is a visualization artifact intended for technical audiences, but it does not itself establish the underlying theory. The script is coherent and admissible as a visualization tool, but its claims of rigor are not proven by the visualizations alone.
